title: KPI trajectory stewardship and readiness log
content:
Purpose: Single-sheet working tracker that combines a directional KPI runway, ownership handoffs, and a practical pre-launch checklist for any product-ops scoped activation (beta, staged rollout, GA). Use as the canonical short-form for launch readiness syncs and as the artifact attached to go/no-go threads.

Notes to self (working): keep rows minimal; avoid duplicating metric definitions from Confluence; link to canonical evals for quality signals. This is deliberately lightweight for 15-minute launch readiness standups.

INSTRUCTIONS:
- Owner maintains cells through rollout phases: planning -> alpha -> beta -> ramp -> GA -> steady-state.
- Color convention (informal): red = failing gate, yellow = borderline, green = on-target.
- When a metric flips red, ping the on-call runbook channel and fill "action taken" in the row.

Tracker (row-oriented):
1) Initiative: "Smart Prompt Routing" (short desc: route requests to cheaper/compatible variants based on policy threshold)
   - Primary owner: Aisha Khan
   - Secondary: Benji Morales (infra)
   - Leading metric: median p95 inference latency (ms) per route
   - Target (ramp->GA): p95 < 120ms for 95% of traffic, median < 45ms
   - Quality guardrail: generation F1 on safety/regression evals >= 0.92 relative to baseline
   - Cost target: average token cost < $0.0012 per generated token for routed traffic
   - Rollout gate: must pass canary for both latency and regression checks for 72 hours with no outages
   - Prelaunch checklist (short): baseline A/B test ready, fallbacks configured, telemetry tags in place
   - Postlaunch monitoring: stream p95, error-rate, fallback-rate to Console dashboard; synthetic traffic every 10m
   - Fallback plan: immediate route to non-routed default variant + scale up capacity; notify oncall and product-ops lead

2) Initiative: "Default Dedicated Pool (Tiered)"
   - Primary owner: Clara Chen
   - Leading metric: request throughput (RPS) capacity utilization and queueing delay
   - Target: < 60% sustained utilization during first 30 days at expected load; queueing delay < 50ms
   - SLA gate: dedicated pool must meet latency SLO in 99.9% of requests for 7-day window in staging
   - Prelaunch: capacity commit docs, infra runbook validated, autoscale test complete
   - Postlaunch: hourly capacity burn chart plus daily cost reconciliation
   - Rollback: migrate customers back to hosted API with throttles; trigger sales/CS comms playbook

3) Initiative: "Optimize: Quantization Profile Rollout"
   - Owner: Diego Rivera
   - Leading metric: model quality regression delta (BLEU/ROUGE or model-specific eval) and inference cost/w throughput
   - Target: regression <= 1.5% on critical prompts; throughput improvement >= 2x for quantized variant
   - Safety gate: must pass adversarial prompt set and hallucination checks
   - Prelaunch: publish model registry entry, quantization profile validated on representative input distribution
   - Postlaunch: nightly spot-check sampling and drift alerting

Common readiness checklist (apply to every row above before moving phases):
- [ ] Product spec and customer impact doc linked in row
- [ ] Alerting: latency, errors, fallback-rate, cost burn (owner must confirm)
- [ ] Telemetry tags exist and mapped to Console (route, model, commitment tier)
- [ ] Canary plan: traffic % and duration defined (usually 1-5% for 48-72h)
- [ ] Rollback triggers defined with owners and SLAs
- [ ] Customer comms draft (if external) or internal stakeholder note (if internal-facing)
- [ ] Security review complete for Private/Dedicated dependencies
- [ ] Legal/Compliance notified when PII or regulated data used
- [ ] SRE & infra runbook link present and validated in a dry-run

Launch decision heuristics (short):
- Proceed to wider rollout when: all green on primary metrics for 72 hours, no production regressions, fallback rate < 0.5%
- Hold and remediate when: any primary metric is red for >2 monitoring cycles or a regression is detected on quality evals
- Abort and rollback when: persistent customer-impacting errors OR security issues OR cost overruns >40% relative to forecasted burn

Signal definitions (for quick-sync):
- Primary metric: the metric that most directly ties to user experience and business impact (latency, correctness, cost)
- Secondary signals: infra health, queueing, error surface, fallback-rate, support tickets
- Quality signal: regression checks vs baseline prompt set + safety suite results

On-call & escalation (practical):
- Level 0: owner and secondary (immediate action, usually < 15m)
- Level 1: product-ops lead + SRE (escalation if incident > 30m or customer-visible)
- Level 2: Eng director + Head of Product (escalate for cross-team impact or legal exposure)
- Channels: #prodops-launches (async updates), #infra-oncall (page when outage), Zoom bridge if incident declared

Runbook snippets (pasteable on incident):
1) Declare incident with prefix "LAUNCH-IMPACT-<initiative>" and list current suspect metric
2) Toggle canary to 0% (if running) or flip routing to default variant
3) Re-run quick health checks: synthetic request set, latency histogram, tail errors
4) If regression, revert to previous model variant or disable new optimization flag
5) Notify stakeholders (CS, sales, security) with summary and next steps

Weekly cadence for this doc:
- Monday: owner updates metric points and notes (quick 10m sync)
- Wednesday: product-ops weekly readout includes top 3 items from this sheet
- Friday: postmortem/lessons (if any changes hit red during week)

Open questions (for next sync):
- What threshold do we want for fallback-rate before proactively throttling (propose 1%)?
- How to standardize the cost per-token micro-metrics across teams for consistent comparison?
- Do we need a separate security gating row for Private deploys requiring HSM integration?

Quick links (for owner use):
- Canary policy doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Canary+Policy
- Telemetry onboarding guide: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/METRICS/Telemetry+Onboarding
- Billing forecast sheet: PRODBILL-forecast-2025 (linked in tracker)

Change log (short):
- 2025-01-15: initial draft created by Aisha Khan
- 2025-01-22: added quantization rollout row (Diego) and checklist items for security
- 2025-02-10: updated rollout gates and cadence per product-ops retro
